faq.q: Is Downtown an official City of Vancouver area, and is the West End part of it?
faq.a: Downtown is one of the City's 22 distinct local areas; the West End is a separate official local area west of Downtown and is not part of Downtown.

Yaletown and Gastown sit inside the Downtown local area; the Downtown Eastside and Chinatown need qualification — the City's Strathcona page states Strathcona includes the Downtown Eastside, at the east side of the Downtown local area.

faq.q: Which schools are located in Downtown?
faq.a: Two VSB elementaries — Elsie Roy, 150 Drake Street, and Crosstown šxʷwəq̓ʷəθət, 55 Expo Boulevard; no public secondary school inside the area was confirmed in this pass, and catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the VSB locator.

faq.q: What zoning governs most of Downtown?
faq.a: The Downtown District (DD) schedule in By-law 3575, which permits the uses set out in the Downtown District Official Development Plan — commercial, residential, institutional and light industrial uses, parks and open spaces, and public uses — with CD-1 and C-3A districts also applying in parts of the area.

faq.q: What shoreline and heritage checks apply in Downtown?
faq.a: The City's designated floodplain includes the False Creek coastal floodplain, with by-law setback and flood construction level requirements for parcels in it, and the City's heritage areas work gives regulations for Gastown, Chinatown and Yaletown at and beside the area's east and south sides; a specific parcel's status must be checked in the City dataset.
